study: E0a - memory-verb base rate over the pinned transcript corpus (offline)
form: APPENDED, never a rewrite. preregistration.json is left byte-identical and its digest above still verifies against preregistration.sha256. This file is the recorded deviation; analysis.json carries both digests so a published number names the exact rule set that produced it.
trigger: Review of the first analysis run reproduced two measurement defects that invalidate every number it published. Both are recorded here rather than fixed silently in the locked clause.

deviations.locked_text: a write is UNAMBIGUOUS when it carries an explicit --key flag or at least two positionals. A single-positional write is AMBIGUOUS.
deviations.amended_rule: a write is UNAMBIGUOUS if and only if it carries an explicit key flag (--key / -k). Every write with no key flag is AMBIGUOUS, whatever its positional count. No positional is ever read as a key.
deviations.reason: The locked rule inferred a bare-key write form that the shipped CLI does not have. `bd remember --help` on the host build (bd 1.3.0-rc.1) states: 'The positional arg is the memory CONTENT (the key is auto-generated from it unless --key is given)', and 'if the arg is a bare key naming an existing memory, it is RECALLED instead of stored'. So a positional never names a memory being stored, and a two-positional write does not resolve into key-plus-content. The locked rule's rationale rested on a grammar the CLI contradicts.
deviations.consequence: Writes move from the band's low end to its high end. The band still brackets the same total write count; what changes is how many writes can supply a key to the E0.4 join, which is strictly fewer.
deviations.not_done: preregistration.json is not edited. Its ambiguity_band clause stands as the record of what was locked before the CLI was checked.

deviations.locked_text: each is shlex-parsed into argv, wrapper and env-assignment tokens are stripped
deviations.amended_rule: shell redirections are stripped from the raw simple-command text, by a quote-aware scan, BEFORE shlex tokenization.
deviations.reason: The sealed helper matched a redirection only as a bare operator token. shlex emits an attached redirection as ONE token ('2>/dev/null'), which that test misses, so the redirection target survived into argv and was counted as a POSITIONAL. The first run called 21 writes unambiguous: 11 by explicit key flag, 10 by the locked bare-key rule alone. Nine of those 10 owe their second positional to a redirect target, and all 10 are `bd remember --show <key>` or `bd remember --get <key>`, which are attempted reads. No token-level test can repair this: once shlex has discarded quoting, a redirection token and a quoted '>' inside a memory body are indistinguishable, so the strip has to run on text that still carries its quotes.
deviations.consequence: Positional counts fall for every redirected invocation. Combined with A1.1 this removes the sole read-after-write hit the first run reported: it was `bd remember --get <term> 2>/dev/null`, an ATTEMPTED READ whose redirection target was counted as content and whose first positional was then read as a key, joined to a `bd recall <term>` four seconds later. The corrected join is 0/16, not 1/16. (`--get` is not a flag of the shipped `bd remember`; the corrected rule keeps it out of the join without needing to know what it meant, because it carries no key flag.)

deviations.supersedes: exclusions (ordering only; no exclusion is added or removed)
deviations.amended_rule: the locked-timestamp self-exclusion is screened BEFORE the help and placeholder exclusions.
deviations.reason: The first run screened help and placeholder invocations first, so post-lock traffic could still move those counts: the help count went 964 -> 966 between two runs over a growing corpus. A published exclusion count must be a property of the pinned population, not of when the script was run.
deviations.consequence: Exactly one exclusion count can now grow with the corpus (after_preregistration_lock), and the emitted artifact separates it from the frozen ones. Counted invocations are unaffected.

unchanged: the verb table and the three-way read split
the ZFC boundary: no argument body is inspected anywhere
the three declared deviations from the sealed selector-expressibility profile
sealed_package_untouched: results/bdp/selector-expressibility/ is not modified. Its manifest digests still verify; the helpers used here are copies.
